Brought to you in association with The Model Railway Club and World of Railways, the 2026 event promises to be the biggest and best yet — showcasing the artistry, precision, and innovation that make railway modelling such a beloved pastime. Visitors can look forward to over 90 leading trade stands featuring tools, kits, scenery, and accessories, as well as 40+ inspiring layouts from top modellers across multiple gauges and eras.

description: At the Romsey & District Railway Modellers Society will be holding their 46th Annual exhibition in the Crosfield Hall, Broadwater Road, Romsey. The aim of the exhibition is to show a cross section of the hobby with a variety of gauges, so there is something for everyone! Each year the Society makes donations to local charities and this year presentations totalling £1,000 will be made. Refreshments will be available both days. Admission: Adults £7, Children (5-16) £3, Family (2 + 2) £17. Parking is available at the Hall and there is FREE car parking on Sunday.

With more than 4000 visitors over 2 days, the show features traders, society stands, and layouts covering most common gauges. The event is hosted by the Abingdon & District Model Railway Club (registered charity 1176029).

Pre-paid discounted tickets are available until Good Friday. A company limited by guarantee (Company number 10369624), the show is known as the best in railway modelling and takes place every Easter.

description: A model railway exhibition featuring 17 layouts in various scales (OO, N, HO, O-16.5), 12 traders, societies, and demonstrators. The show includes layouts ranging from British heritage railways to American and German themes, spanning different eras from the 1950s to present day. Special attractions include a Thomas-themed children's layout where young visitors can become engine drivers with certificates, live demonstrations of weathering techniques, loco maintenance clinic, and cardboard model making. Traders offer new and pre-owned models, railway books, accessories, and custom items. Society stands represent the Great Central Railway, Great Northern Railway Society, and others. Some areas accessible only via steps.
